description: DEF CON 31 Main Stage features flagship research, keynotes, and presentations spanning firmware and hardware reverse engineering, advanced operating system exploitation, cloud and identity vulnerabilities, AI red teaming, and landmark cybersecurity policy discussions.

talks.title: Infinite Money Glitch: Hacking Transit Cards
talks.teaser: Four high school researchers reverse engineer Boston's CharlieCard RFID fare system, uncovering cryptographic flaws and building a portable fare machine.
talks.summary:
Reverse Engineering Legacy Transit Smartcards

Municipal public transit systems rely on contactless RFID smartcards to store value and process turnstile entries, but many legacy implementations use outdated cryptographic architectures.

Analyzing Boston's CharlieCard Architecture

Four high school security researchers dissect the hardware and proprietary memory structure of the Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority (MBTA) CharlieCard system, exploring legacy MIFARE card structures.

Building Custom Emulation and Portable Fare Tools

By intercepting card-reader exchanges and decoding stored balance blocks, the team developed custom hardware emulators and a portable fare modification device.

Responsible Disclosure to Government Agencies

The speakers recount their experience responsibly disclosing the vulnerabilities to the transit authority, sharing lessons for student researchers navigating vulnerability disclosure.

talks.title: An Audacious Plan to Halt the Internet's Enshittification
talks.teaser: Cory Doctorow analyzes platform decay across Big Tech monopolies and outlines a policy and technical roadmap for interoperability, privacy, and user self-help.
talks.summary:
The Mechanics of Platform Decay

Cory Doctorow dissects 'enshittification', the lifecycle where dominant platforms first lure users with subsidies, exploit those users to attract business customers, and ultimately claw back all surplus value for shareholders.

Monopolistic Consolidation and Legal Barriers

Decades of unchecked corporate mergers have consolidated the web into a handful of walled gardens, reinforced by anti-reverse-engineering laws and draconian digital rights management (DRM) statutes.

Antitrust, Interoperability, and Regulatory Reform

Halting platform degradation requires aggressive antitrust enforcement, robust privacy frameworks, and legal mandates for adversarial interoperability that prevent vendor lock-in.

Empowering User-Side Technical Self-Help

Doctorow champions grassroots technical resistance—including sideloading, alternative app stores, web scrapers, and ad-blocking—to restore user autonomy across digital ecosystems.

talks.title: Demystifying (and Bypassing) macOS's Background Task Management
talks.teaser: Patrick Wardle dissects macOS Ventura's Background Task Management architecture, releasing open-source tooling while demonstrating trivial evasion techniques.
talks.summary:
Rearchitecting Persistence in macOS Ventura

Malware relies on persistence mechanisms to maintain execution across system reboots. In macOS Ventura, Apple introduced Background Task Management (BTM) to alert users to persistent items.

Reverse Engineering BTM Internals and SQLite Stores

Patrick Wardle explores the undocumented daemon architecture, private XPC endpoints, and internal databases that macOS uses to track LaunchDaemons, LaunchAgents, and login items.

Open-Source Enumeration Tooling for Forensics

Because Apple's proprietary framework broke existing heuristic detection pipelines, Wardle releases open-source tools to programmatically extract and inspect all registered persistent items.

Trivially Bypassing BTM Alerts

Analyzing subtle design oversights in user notification handling demonstrates how malicious binaries can silently install persistent launch components without triggering security alerts.

talks.title: The Internals of Veilid: A New Decentralized Application Framework
talks.teaser: Cult of the Dead Cow introduces Veilid, an open-source Rust-based peer-to-peer framework for building private, metadata-resistant applications without blockchains.
talks.summary:
Designing a Blockchain-Free Decentralized Framework

Veilid is an open-source, mobile-first peer-to-peer framework engineered to provide encrypted, metadata-protected communication and decentralized storage without relying on blockchains or central servers.

Cryptographic Foundations and Private Routing

DilDog and Medus4 detail Veilid's Rust architecture, which leverages end-to-end encryption, onion-style private routing routes, and distributed hash tables optimized for low latency and high node churn.

Resilient Multi-Protocol Networking

Veilid operates across UDP, TCP, WebSockets, and WASM, featuring dynamic transport switching that maintains seamless connections during cellular-to-Wi-Fi handoffs.

Building Applications on Veilid

The authors demonstrate Veilid Server alongside VeilidChat, showcasing how developers can build secure messaging and decentralized applications atop the network.

talks.title: Clocks Have Ears: Timing and Browser-Based Local Network Port Scanner
talks.teaser: Demonstrates browser-based internal network port scanning using precise JavaScript timing side-channels to map intranet devices without elevated privileges.
talks.summary:
In this presentation on the DEF CON 31 Main Stage, researcher Donny Kim presents "Clocks Have Ears," revealing how high-resolution browser timing APIs can be weaponized to perform stealthy local network port scans directly through client-side JavaScript. He opens at 03:03 by explaining how measuring precise execution intervals with window.performance.now() during fetch() requests exposes internal network topology without triggering Same-Origin Policy (SOP) blocks.

Donny analyzes network timing signatures at 06:03, demonstrating that closed ports on local hosts reject TCP packets within fractions of a millisecond, whereas open ports or filtered IP addresses experience measurable delays or timeouts. At 09:04, he presents empirical timing graphs establishing 50-millisecond detection thresholds across private subnets (10.0.0.1, 192.168.1.1). At 15:00, he demonstrates a working web-based port scanner that maps local services (AirPlay, Discord RPC) within minutes, concluding at 17:00 with browser security defenses including timer quantization and Private Network Access (PNA) specifications. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Weaponizing Plain Text: ANSI Escape Sequences as a Forensic Nightmare
talks.teaser: STÖK demonstrates how malicious ANSI escape codes can weaponize application logs to deceive incident responders and compromise modern DevOps terminal emulators.
talks.summary:
The Hidden Risk of ANSI Escape Codes in Logs

Application log files are universally trusted by system administrators and SOC analysts, yet parsing untrusted inputs containing raw terminal control characters creates severe injection risks.

From Legacy Terminal Tricks to Modern Cloud CLIs

STÖK revisits historical 1980s terminal injection vulnerabilities, showing how modern cloud CLIs, CI/CD pipelines, and feature-rich terminal emulators remain susceptible to screen-clearing and cursor-manipulation tricks.

Fabricating Forensic Evidence and Masking Intrusions

Adversaries can embed carefully formatted escape sequences into web server requests to overwrite log lines, spoof forensic timestamps, and conceal unauthorized administrative actions.

Sanitization and Defensive Hardening

Implementing strict output sanitization, stripping unprintable control bytes before logging, and configuring hardened terminal viewers protects security teams during incident response.

talks.title: Warshopping: Phreaking Smart Shopping Cart Wheels Through RF Sniffing
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers electronic shopping cart containment wheels, capturing ultra-low-frequency and 2.4 GHz RF signals to unlock wheel braking mechanisms.
talks.summary:
Containment Systems in Smart Shopping Carts

Retailers deploy electronic cart wheels with integrated mechanical brakes to prevent cart theft, triggering locking mechanisms via subterranean low-frequency perimeter coils.

Sniffing Ultra-Low-Frequency and 2.4 GHz Signals

Joseph Gabay analyzes the Rocateq smart wheel system, capturing perimeter boundary signals and 2.4 GHz register checkout broadcasts using software-defined radio.

Hardware Teardown and Firmware Extraction

Soldering test leads onto the wheel's internal PCB enables logic analyzer tracing of chip-to-chip serial buses, while a PICkit programmer dumps firmware for Ghidra analysis.

Simulating Control Codes via Audio Transducers

Because the wheel coils respond to low-frequency magnetic modulation, Gabay demonstrates triggering and disarming cart wheel locks directly from a smartphone speaker.

talks.title: Visual Studio Code is Why I Have Workspace Trust Issues
talks.teaser: Uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities in Visual Studio Code, demonstrating how malicious repository configurations bypass Workspace Trust protections.
talks.summary:
Targeting Developers Through Code Editors

Modern Integrated Development Environments (IDEs) possess deep system integration and automatic extension execution, making developer workstations prime targets for nation-state threat actors.

Deconstructing VS Code's Workspace Trust Boundary

Thomas Chauchefoin and Paul Gerste evaluate Microsoft's Workspace Trust model, analyzing how restricted execution modes attempt to shield developers when opening untrusted repositories.

Chaining CVE-2021-43891 and CVE-2022-30129 to RCE

Dissecting two distinct vulnerabilities reveals how malicious workspace configuration files and vulnerable extension parsers allow remote code execution upon simply cloning a project.

Hardening Development Environments

The researchers present actionable recommendations for IDE developers and engineering teams to audit extension trust boundaries and secure developer toolchains.

talks.title: Video-Based Cryptanalysis: Extracting Keys from Power LEDs
talks.teaser: Recovers cryptographic keys by analyzing video footage of device power LEDs, using camera rolling shutters to measure CPU power consumption fluctuations.
talks.summary:
Optical Side-Channels via Power LEDs

Cryptographic operations induce subtle power consumption fluctuations within processors, which instantaneously alter the brightness and color spectrum emitted by device power indicator LEDs.

High-Frequency Sampling via Camera Rolling Shutters

Ben Nassi and Ofek Vayner demonstrate that commercial video cameras with rolling shutters can sample LED luminosity across individual sensor scan lines, boosting effective optical sampling rates by 1000x.

Extracting 256-Bit ECDSA and SIKE Keys at Distance

Experimental validations demonstrate extracting a 256-bit ECDSA private key from a smartcard reader from 16 meters away via a security camera, and recovering post-quantum SIKE keys from smartphone peripherals.

Countermeasures and Physical Mitigations

Mitigating optical cryptanalysis requires hardware filtering capacitors, constant-current LED drivers, physical light diffusers, and constant-time cryptographic libraries.

talks.title: Vacuum Robot Security & Privacy: Prevent Your Robot from Sucking Your Data
talks.teaser: Dennis Giese demonstrates rooting flagship robotic vacuum cleaners across four vendors, exposing cloud telemetry risks and enabling offline open-source control.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of Sensors in Smart Vacuums

Modern robotic vacuum cleaners have evolved from simple bump-and-go devices to networked camera- and microphone-equipped IoT platforms running embedded Linux and computer vision models.

Rooting Flagship Vacuum Models Across Four Vendors

Dennis Giese walks through hardware debugging interfaces, bootloader modifications, and flash memory extraction techniques to achieve root shell access on commercial vacuums.

Auditing Data Privacy and Cloud Telemetry

Inspecting filesystem contents and network traffic reveals extensive telemetry, including unencrypted floor plans, ambient audio recordings, and room photos streamed to vendor cloud servers.

Reclaiming Hardware via Open-Source Firmware

Deploying custom open-source software platforms like Valetudo enables homeowners to disconnect their vacuum robots from cloud servers while retaining full autonomous cleaning functionality.

talks.title: Unlocking Hidden Powers in Xtensa-Based Qualcomm Wi-Fi Chips
talks.teaser: Extends the Nexmon firmware modification framework to Xtensa-based Qualcomm Wi-Fi chipsets, enabling custom frame injection and security research.
talks.summary:
Closed-Source Microcontrollers in Wireless Silicon

Modern Wi-Fi chipsets rely on high-performance embedded processor cores running proprietary, closed-source firmware that restricts low-level radio manipulation.

Architecture of Qualcomm Xtensa Wi-Fi Processors

Daniel Wegemer analyzes the Xtensa processor architecture and internal firmware structures deployed inside modern Qualcomm wireless system-on-chips.

Porting Nexmon to Xtensa Firmware

Extending the open-source Nexmon patching framework to Xtensa binaries provides automated hooks and compilation toolchains to inject C code directly into wireless firmware.

Enabling Advanced Wireless Research

Custom firmware patches allow security researchers to enable monitor mode, raw packet injection, and low-level 802.11 frame fuzzing on commodity hardware.

talks.title: Unlocking Doors from Half a Continent Away
talks.teaser: Demonstrates long-distance relay attacks against ISO 14443A and HID SEOS contactless credentials, unlocking a physical door in Ottawa from a stage in Las Vegas.
talks.summary:
Weaknesses in Contactless RFID Timing Windows

Contactless smartcard protocols rely on proximity assumptions, but protocol timing tolerances often allow communications to be relayed over long-distance network connections.

Deconstructing ISO 14443A and HID SEOS Relays

Trevor Stevado and Sam Haskins analyze timing parameters in the ISO 14443A standard that permit packet forwarding across moderate-latency internet links without triggering reader timeouts.

Live Long-Distance Door Unlock Demonstration

Using custom Proxmark firmware and network bridging software, the presenters execute a live relay attack, presenting a badge in Las Vegas to unlock an HID SEOS door lock located in Ottawa.

Defensive Architecture and Reader Mitigations

Mitigating contactless relay attacks requires configuring strict protocol timeout thresholds, implementing multi-factor authentication, and adopting location-aware mobile credentials.

talks.title: UNConventional Cybercrime: Bad Treaty Becoming Law
talks.teaser: EFF experts analyze the draft UN Cybercrime Treaty, warning of risks to security research, vulnerability disclosure, and global human rights.
talks.summary:
Negotiating the UN Cybercrime Treaty

The United Nations has drafted a comprehensive global cybercrime treaty that risks reshaping international anti-hacking legal standards and cross-border surveillance agreements.

Threats to Legitimate Security Research

Katitza Rodriguez and Bill Budington highlight the treaty's broad definitions of unauthorized access, which lack explicit safe harbor protections for ethical hackers, penetration testers, and bug bounty hunters.

Human Rights and Surveillance Overreach

The proposed framework grants governments expansive powers for cross-border electronic evidence sharing and digital surveillance without robust procedural safeguards.

Advocacy and Community Action in Vienna

EFF delegates report from the treaty negotiations in Vienna, calling on the global hacker community to demand explicit researcher exemptions in final treaty ratifications.

talks.title: Turning My Virtual Wallet into a Skimming Device
talks.teaser: Examines hardware and Bluetooth vulnerabilities in low-cost Mobile Point-of-Sale (MPOS) card readers that allow attackers to skim payment credentials.
talks.summary:
The Proliferation of Mobile Point-of-Sale Hardware

In emerging economies, low-cost Mobile Point-of-Sale (MPOS) card readers paired with smartphones have become the dominant infrastructure for processing contactless and chip transactions.

Hardware Teardowns and Microcontroller Extraction

Federico Borgogno and Luciano Barrionuevo dissect budget MPOS readers, analyzing microcontroller security, PCB trace routing, and anti-tamper mesh failures.

Exploiting Bluetooth Communication Flaws

Insecure pairing mechanisms and unencrypted serial communication between the terminal and host smartphone enable man-in-the-middle interception of payment data.

Constructing Virtual Skimming Devices

Demonstrating arbitrary firmware modification and malicious companion apps shows how rogue merchants or attackers can silently capture payment card data during routine sales.

talks.title: Track the Planet! Mapping IDs & Monitoring Presence in Azure
talks.teaser: Alexander Hagenah details unauthenticated, zero-log user enumeration techniques across Microsoft Azure, Teams, and OneDrive spanning millions of accounts.
talks.summary:
Silent Reconnaissance in Cloud Directories

Reconnaissance against enterprise cloud environments typically generates audit logs, but subtle API design behaviors in Microsoft Azure permit silent, zero-log account discovery.

Unauthenticated Enumeration via OneDrive and Teams

Alexander Hagenah reveals how querying OneDrive endpoints and unauthenticated Microsoft Teams presence lookup APIs reveals valid usernames without triggering logon events or failed authentication logs.

Mapping Enterprise Adoption and Online Presence

Demonstrating datasets of over 20 million enumerated accounts illustrates how telemetry from out-of-office messages and Teams status indicators enables organizational mapping at scale.

Discovering Hidden Cross-Tenant Relationships

Exploiting Azure Guest collaboration metadata uncovers hidden business partnerships and joint venture relationships between distinct corporate tenants.

talks.title: There Are No Mushroom Clouds in Cyberwar
talks.teaser: Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense Mieke Eoyang debunks nuclear analogies in cyberwarfare, detailing modern Defend Forward strategies and public-private partnerships.
talks.summary:
Deconstructing the Nuclear Myth in Cyber Conflict

Popular culture and early defense theorizing frequently drew analogies between nuclear deterrence and cyber operations, stoking fears of catastrophic 'Cyber Pearl Harbor' scenarios.

The Ephemeral Nature of Cyber Operations

Mieke Eoyang analyzes the operational reality of cyber capabilities, emphasizing that cyber effects are difficult to attribute, rarely permanently decisive, and require continuous adaptation.

The Evolution to Defending Forward

The United States defense strategy shifted from passive deterrence to 'Defending Forward', actively disrupting adversary operations abroad before they impact domestic critical infrastructure.

Lessons from Conventional Warfare and Private Collaboration

Conflict in Ukraine demonstrates the crucial importance of private industry resilience, commercial threat intelligence, and independent security researcher collaborations in national defense.

talks.title: Ringhopper: How We Almost Zero-Day'd the World
talks.teaser: Benny Zeltser and Jonathan Lusky detail RingHopper, a multi-vendor UEFI vulnerability allowing user-space attackers to jump directly into System Management Mode (SMM).
talks.summary:
The Crown Jewels of System Management Mode

System Management Mode (SMM) is the most privileged execution ring in x86 architecture, executing underneath the operating system kernel and hypervisor with direct access to physical memory.

Discovering Industry-Wide EDK2 Flaws

Benny Zeltser and Jonathan Lusky uncover RingHopper, a pervasive family of vulnerabilities across major UEFI firmware implementations affecting billions of commercial devices.

Engineering the Leap from User-Land to Ring -2

The researchers detail the exploitation chain, manipulating SMI handlers and EDK2 memory structures to escalate privileges from unprivileged user-space directly into SMM.

Coordinated Disclosure and Firmware Hardening

Working with over eight major hardware vendors to coordinate firmware patches highlights the systemic difficulty of remediating low-level firmware flaws at global scale.

talks.title: How Vulns in Global Transportation Payment Systems Cost You
talks.teaser: Omer Attias dissects API vulnerabilities in popular mobile transit payment apps like Moovit, demonstrating fare evasion and passenger PII data leakage.
talks.summary:
The Rise of Mobile Public Transit Ticketing

Transit agencies worldwide have rapidly adopted smartphone applications to streamline fare payments, ticket validations, and route planning across thousands of metropolitan areas.

Reverse Engineering the Moovit Mobile API

Omer Attias audits the API backend of Moovit, a mobility application serving hundreds of millions of users across 100+ countries, inspecting encrypted mobile traffic.

Exploiting Fare Validation and Payment Logic

Flaws in ticket issuance endpoints and authorization tokens allow malicious actors to generate valid transit passes without charge and manipulate billing assignments onto third-party accounts.

Harvesting Passenger Personally Identifiable Information

Insecure direct object references (IDOR) in passenger profiles allowed unauthorized extraction of customer PII, highlighting critical security requirements for smart city infrastructure.

talks.title: DARPA AI Cyber Challenge Announcement
talks.teaser: DARPA Program Manager Perri Adams and industry leaders announce the AI Cyber Challenge (AIxCC) to automate software vulnerability discovery and remediation.
talks.summary:
DARPA program manager Perri Adams is joined by industry and open-source leaders on the DEF CON 31 Main Stage to formally announce the launch of the AI Cyber Challenge (AIxCC).

[00:03] Adams introduces the initiative, which pairs DARPA with leading AI research laboratories—including Anthropic, Google, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI—alongside the Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF). The two-year competition is designed to develop novel Cyber Reasoning Systems (CRSs) that integrate advanced artificial intelligence and large language models with automated program analysis [09:20] to secure critical open-source software infrastructure.

[13:22] The panelists discuss the technical vision of AIxCC: moving beyond manual vulnerability research to create autonomous systems that can discover complex software vulnerabilities, verify exploitability, and automatically generate and test verified source code patches. Adams outlines the competition structure and substantial prize pool [17:27], featuring over $20 million in funding culminating in finals at DEF CON 33, inviting global security researchers and AI practitioners to participate.

talks.title: The Hackers, The Lawyers, And The Defense Fund
talks.teaser: EFF attorneys and security researchers discuss legal defense strategies and introduce the Security Research Legal Defense Fund for good-faith hackers.
talks.summary:
Legal Perils Facing Good-Faith Security Researchers

Security researchers routinely face aggressive legal threats, civil lawsuits, and criminal statutes from software vendors attempting to suppress vulnerability disclosure.

Providing Pro Bono Legal Counseling for Hackers

Kurt Opsahl and legal advocates explain how the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF) counsels security researchers prior to publication to mitigate legal exposure.

Introducing the Security Research Legal Defense Fund

The panel announces the launch of the Security Research Legal Defense Fund, an independent initiative providing legal representation funding to hackers facing litigation.

Navigating Coordinated Disclosure and Rights

Panelists share practical guidance for handling cease-and-desist letters, communicating with corporate counsel, and advancing researcher protections worldwide.

talks.title: The GitHub Actions Worm
talks.teaser: Asi Greenholts demonstrates a proof-of-concept worm propagating through the GitHub Actions ecosystem by compromising interdependent custom actions.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of GitHub Actions in CI/CD

GitHub Actions has become the backbone of modern open-source software deployment, executing automated build, test, and release workflows with access to sensitive repository secrets.

Analyzing Implicit Dependency Trees in Custom Actions

Asi Greenholts demonstrates how custom GitHub Actions create complex, implicit dependency chains where workflows rely on third-party actions without strict SHA-pinning.

Engineering a Self-Replicating Pipeline Worm

Compromising a single vulnerable upstream action allows an attacker to manipulate runner execution environments, inject malicious payload code into downstream actions, and propagate across repositories.

Hardening Workflows Against Supply Chain Propagation

Defending CI/CD pipelines requires enforcing strict commit SHA pinning for third-party actions, implementing least-privilege token permissions, and monitoring runner process spawns.

talks.title: TETRA Tour de Force: Jailbreaking Digital Radios & Base Stations for Fun
talks.teaser: Midnight Blue reverse engineers the secret TETRA radio standard, uncovering proprietary cipher flaws and a backdoored encryption algorithm in critical infrastructure.
talks.summary:
The Secrecy of Terrestrial Trunked Radio (TETRA)

TETRA is the global digital radio standard utilized by police, military agencies, and critical infrastructure SCADA telecontrol for oil pipelines and electrical grids.

Reverse Engineering the TI OMAP-L138 TEE and DSP

Midnight Blue details jailbreaking the Motorola MTM5x00 radio by chaining zero-day vulnerabilities, hardware side-channel attacks, and custom decompilers across trusted execution environments.

Uncovering Flaws in TEA Ciphers and Backdoors

Extracting the proprietary TEA1 through TEA4 cipher suites for the first time revealed critical vulnerabilities, including an intentionally backdoored stream cipher with reduced entropy.

Instrumenting Motorola Base Stations and Mitigations

Demonstrating live packet decryption and traffic injection using an instrumented Motorola MBTS base station provides operators with crucial firmware mitigation guidance.

talks.title: Terminally Owned: 60 Years of Escaping
talks.teaser: David Leadbeater revisits 60 years of terminal escape sequence vulnerabilities, detailing multiple remote code execution flaws across major terminal emulators.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Terminal Emulators

Since the publication of ASCII 60 years ago, terminal emulators have processed control characters and escape sequences to handle text formatting and window manipulation.

Revisiting Historical Terminal Injection Flaws

Building upon classic research by HD Moore, David Leadbeater audits half a dozen modern terminal emulators across Linux, macOS, and Windows to uncover parsing vulnerabilities.

Chaining Control Sequences to Remote Code Execution

Demonstrating malicious terminal sequences shows how viewing untrusted log files or running command-line tools can trigger arbitrary code execution in the context of the user.

Hardening Terminal Emulation Standards

Remediating terminal vulnerabilities requires disabling hazardous legacy escape sequences, enforcing strict parser boundaries, and validating user input in CLI tooling.

talks.title: Still Vulnerable Out of the Box
talks.teaser: Audits 21 prepaid and 11 unlocked Android smartphones, uncovering privilege escalation, arbitrary file access, and remote command execution in preloaded firmware.
talks.summary:
The Persistent Risks of Prepaid Smartphones

Prepaid Android smartphones sold by major carriers offer affordable hardware, but frequently ship with bloated, unvetted pre-installed software from carriers, chipset vendors, and third parties.

Auditing 32 Carrier and Unlocked Android Devices

Ryan Johnson, Mohamed Elsabagh, and Angelos Stavrou examine the local attack surface across 21 prepaid carrier devices and 11 unlocked handsets purchased from retail stores.

Exploiting Insecure Local Interfaces and Pre-Loaded Apps

Unprivileged third-party apps can exploit unprotected BroadcastReceivers and ContentProviders to execute arbitrary system commands, trigger factory resets, and exfiltrate GPS location data.

Systemic Supply Chain and OEM Accountability

The findings demonstrate systemic failures in OEM and carrier firmware quality control, urging regulators and vendors to enforce strict privilege boundaries on pre-installed applications.

talks.title: Spread Spectrum Techniques for Anti-Drone Evasion
talks.teaser: Explores implementing low-cost frequency-hopping spread spectrum algorithms on DIY and consumer drones to resist RF jamming and anti-drone interception.
talks.summary:
RF Warfare Against Consumer and DIY Drones

Commercial and hobbyist unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) increasingly face electronic warfare countermeasures, where targeted RF jamming disrupts control links and GPS navigation.

Frequency-Hopping Spread Spectrum on Budget Hardware

David Melendez and Gabriela Garcia demonstrate how to implement frequency-hopping spread spectrum (FHSS) on low-cost microcontrollers without requiring expensive precision clocks.

Solving Transmitter-Receiver Synchronization

Developing lightweight software synchronization algorithms allows drone transceivers to rapidly hop frequencies in tandem, maintaining reliable control links amidst electronic interference.

Defeating Anti-Drone Detection and Disruption

Experimental testing demonstrates that agile frequency hopping severely degrades the effectiveness of directional RF jammers and unauthorized drone interception systems.

talks.title: Spooky Authentication at a Distance
talks.teaser: Tamás Jos presents a post-exploitation technique to proxy Windows authentication protocols remotely without elevated privileges, enabling full domain takeover.
talks.summary:
Remote Authentication Proxying in Windows

Traditional credential harvesting requires dumping memory or executing high-privilege code on target machines, often triggering immediate EDR detections.

Unprivileged Post-Exploitation Relay Techniques

Tamás Jos introduces an unprivileged post-exploitation technique that proxies native Windows authentication protocols across remote network connections directly to an operator's workstation.

Complete User Impersonation Without Local Elevated Access

By establishing an authentication bridge, red-team operators can execute actions with the target user's identity across Active Directory services without touching local system credentials.

Zero-Interaction Domain Takeover via Malicious Peripherals

A live demonstration illustrates full domain takeover using a plug-and-play malicious hardware peripheral in a restricted environment without requiring user interaction.

talks.title: SpamChannel: Spoofing Emails from 2M+ Domains
talks.teaser: byt3bl33d3r demonstrates spoofing emails from over two million domains, bypassing SPF and DMARC by exploiting trust architectures between cloud edge services.
talks.summary:
Fragility in Modern Email Authentication

Despite widespread adoption of SPF, DKIM, and DMARC email security records, underlying routing integrations between transactional email providers and cloud edge platforms create critical authentication gaps.

Exploiting Cloudflare and Transactional Email Integrations

byt3bl33d3r analyzes how edge serverless applications interact with major transactional email delivery services, discovering authorization flaws in domain verification pipelines.

Bypassing SPF and DMARC at Global Scale

By abusing shared backend trust boundaries, an attacker can forge cryptographically signed emails appearing from over two million legitimate commercial domains without owning their DNS records.

Tool Release and Mitigation Strategies

The author demonstrates the attack tooling, analyzes the root causes of serverless identity confusion, and provides architectural recommendations for cloud email providers.

talks.title: StackMoonwalk: Advanced Call Stack Tampering and Detection
talks.teaser: Introduces Full Moon and Half Moon call stack spoofing techniques to evade EDR inspection, alongside the Eclipse kernel detection algorithm.
talks.summary:
The Cat-and-Mouse Game of Call Stack Inspection

Modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) sensors analyze thread call stacks during sensitive API calls to identify injected shellcode and unbacked memory execution.

Full Moon and Half Moon Stack Tampering

Alessandro Magnosi, Arash Parsa, and Athanasios Tserpelis present two advanced call stack spoofing techniques that manipulate frame pointer chains to construct unwinding-compliant synthetic stacks.

Defeating Conventional Heuristic Stack Checks

By generating logically valid unwinding sequences, these techniques conceal malicious payload invocation while maintaining thread stability across asynchronous exceptions.

The Eclipse Detection Algorithm

To counter stack spoofing, the authors introduce Eclipse, a detection algorithm extending RtlVirtualUnwind to enforce strict instruction validation and detect tampered execution frames.

talks.title: Snoop on to Them, as They Snoop on to Us
talks.teaser: Investigates fixed-address Bluetooth Low Energy beacons in law enforcement gear, body cameras, and consumer IoT, demonstrating long-term tracking.
talks.summary:
Surveillance and Counter-Surveillance Techniques

This talk examines surveillance methods and counter-surveillance strategies. Topics include how to identify surveillance activities and techniques for protecting privacy and security against observation and tracking.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: Smashing the State Machine: The True Potential of Web Race Conditions
talks.teaser: James Kettle introduces multi-request single-packet race condition techniques, collapsing complex web application state machines within sub-millisecond windows.
talks.summary:
Beyond Simple Limit-Overrun Race Conditions

Web race condition research has historically focused on basic balance duplication, but complex enterprise state machines harbor far deeper synchronization flaws.

Collapsing Application State Machines

James Kettle demonstrates how sending conflicting concurrent inputs can disrupt multi-step workflows, allowing attackers to forge trusted session state, misroute tokens, and bypass authorization.

Single-Packet Attack Methodology

Adapting techniques from HTTP Request Smuggling, Kettle introduces single-packet execution strategies that synchronize dozens of distinct HTTP/2 requests across thousands of miles into a sub-millisecond execution window.

Tooling and Community Research Labs

The presentation releases open-source Burp Suite extensions alongside interactive vulnerability labs to help researchers audit multi-request state transitions.

talks.title: Small Leaks, Billions of Dollars: Cryptographic Attacks on MPC Wallets
talks.teaser: Demonstrates practical cryptographic key-exfiltration attacks against Multi-Party Computation (MPC) algorithms securing billions in cryptocurrency wallets.
talks.summary:
Multi-Party Computation in Digital Asset Custody

Multi-Party Computation (MPC) threshold signatures secure hundreds of billions of dollars across major institutional cryptocurrency exchanges, custody providers, and fintech banks.

Auditing Popular MPC Threshold Protocols

Nikolaos Makriyannis and Oren Yomtov analyze widespread implementations of threshold ECDSA and EdDSA protocols, uncovering subtle cryptographic leakage channels.

Practical Key Exfiltration with Minimal Signatures

The researchers present three distinct cryptographic attacks against different protocol implementations, demonstrating complete private key recovery in 256 signatures, 16 signatures, and a single signature.

Securing Threshold Cryptography Deployments

Remediating MPC vulnerabilities requires strict zero-knowledge proof verification, rigorous parameter validation, and robust fault-injection defenses during distributed key signing.

talks.title: Prototype Pollution Leads to Remote Code Execution in Node.js
talks.teaser: Mikhail Shcherbakov and Musard Balliu uncover universal Prototype Pollution gadgets within Node.js core and popular NPM packages, achieving RCE across major applications.
talks.summary:
Prototype Pollution Beyond Denial of Service

Prototype pollution in JavaScript applications has often been dismissed as a low-severity flaw resulting merely in property injection or denial of service.

Discovering Universal Gadgets in Node.js Core

Mikhail Shcherbakov and Musard Balliu analyze Node.js core libraries and popular NPM dependencies, mapping out universal gadget chains that convert object property modifications into code execution.

Auditing 15 Popular Applications to Yield 8 RCEs

Applying automated static and dynamic analysis across 15 open-source Node.js applications on GitHub yielded 8 high-impact remote code execution zero-days.

Mitigations and Node.js Architectural Hardening

The researchers discuss recent security enhancements in Node.js, including `--disable-proto` flags and defensive coding patterns to prevent prototype poisoning.

talks.title: Second Breakfast: Implicit & Mutation-Based Serialization Vulns in .NET
talks.teaser: Jonathan Birch demonstrates novel .NET deserialization RCE attacks that bypass standard assumptions, exploiting database drivers and immutable data streams.
talks.summary:
Revisiting .NET Deserialization Assumptions

Exploiting insecure deserialization in .NET traditionally assumes that an application explicitly invokes a known dangerous serializer and consumes untrusted, attacker-tampered data streams.

Violating Traditional Exploitation Prerequisites

Jonathan Birch demonstrates novel exploitation techniques where applications neither invoke standard serializers nor receive tampered serialized streams directly.

RCE Vulnerabilities in Leading Database Drivers

Case studies detail remote code execution vulnerabilities discovered in MongoDB, LiteDB, ServiceStack.Redis, RavenDB, MartenDB, JSON.Net, and the .NET JavaScriptSerializer.

Scanning Tools and Modern .NET 6+ Defenses

Birch releases automated vulnerability detection tooling and discusses defensive patterns to eliminate gadget execution in modern .NET core environments.

talks.title: Runtime Riddles: Abusing Manipulation Points in the Android Source
talks.teaser: Laurie Kirk unveils runtime manipulation techniques in native C++ via JNI to alter Android execution flow, defeating emulators and decompilers.
talks.summary:
The Limitations of Static DEX Obfuscation

Traditional Android malware packing and DEX class encryption techniques are increasingly ineffective against modern dynamic analysis sandboxes and automated unpacking tools.

Identifying Runtime Manipulation Points in Android Source

Laurie Kirk details a methodology for locating execution manipulation targets within the Android Open Source Project (AOSP) framework and ART runtime.

Manipulating Java Structures via Native C++ JNI

Hooking Java methods through the Java Native Interface (JNI) and casting method pointers in native memory allows manipulating execution flow without triggering standard ClassLoader hooks.

Breaking Decompiler Cross-References on Android 13

The author releases a custom library targeting Android 13 devices, demonstrating how runtime structure manipulation completely breaks cross-reference calculation in tools like Ghidra and JADX.

talks.title: Route to Bugs: Analyzing the Security of BGP Message Parsing
talks.teaser: Marco dos Santos and Thibault Guiot audit BGP message parsers across seven modern routing implementations, exposing malformed packet vulnerabilities that disrupt transit.
talks.summary:
The Overlooked Attack Surface of BGP Parsers

While internet routing security typically focuses on route hijacking and cryptographic validation via RPKI, implementation bugs in BGP packet parsing remain a critical single point of failure.

Auditing Seven Modern BGP Implementations

Marco dos Santos and Thibault Guiot present a systematic evaluation of seven leading open-source and proprietary BGP routing daemons used in data centers and ISP backbones.

Exploiting Malformed Route Attribute Messages

Fuzzing complex BGP path attributes (such as AS_PATH, communities, and MP-BGP extensions) revealed parsing flaws where a single malformed packet induces daemon crashes or memory corruption.

Hardening Global Internet Routing Software

The authors provide recommendations for protocol developers to implement robust fuzzing pipelines, memory-safe parsers, and defensive validation in core routing infrastructure.

talks.title: Revolutionizing ELF Binary Patching with Shiva
talks.teaser: Ryan O'Neill (ElfMaster) presents Shiva, a revolutionary JIT binary patching system and custom ELF interpreter that loads and links relocatable C patches at runtime.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of ELF Binary Patching

Patching compiled Linux ELF binaries without source code has historically relied on fragile hex editing, text padding injection, or rudimentary binary hooks.

Introducing Shiva: A JIT ELF Interpreter and Linker

Ryan O'Neill (ElfMaster) introduces Shiva, an advanced JIT binary patching system that loads and dynamically links modular C-authored patch files directly into running processes.

Advanced Linker Chaining and Userland Execution

Shiva resurrects classic concepts like userland-exec while introducing novel multi-dynamic-linker chaining, function splicing, and binary transformation capabilities.

Maintaining Insecure Legacy Code and Red-Team Applications

Demonstrations highlight Shiva's dual-use potential: enabling engineers to hot-patch critical security flaws in legacy proprietary binaries while allowing red teams to inject modular in-memory implants.

talks.title: Retro Exploitation: Vintage Computing as a Vulnerability Research Playground
talks.teaser: Wesley McGrew uses Commodore Amiga 16/32-bit vintage computing environments to teach foundational reverse engineering and exploit development using Ghidra.
talks.summary:
Lowering the Barrier to Exploit Development

Modern operating systems feature multi-layered exploit mitigations—such as ASLR, DEP, and CFG—that create an intimidating learning curve for aspiring vulnerability researchers.

Setting Up a Commodore Amiga Research Environment

Wesley McGrew demonstrates how vintage 16/32-bit platforms like the Commodore Amiga provide an accessible, mitigation-free playground for mastering low-level systems concepts.

Reverse Engineering AmigaOS Binaries with Ghidra

Configuring modern Ghidra disassemblers and native Amiga debuggers enables researchers to analyze assembly code, memory layouts, and stack structures in legacy applications.

Case Study: Exploiting a 1994 Amiga FTP Client

A step-by-step case study details the discovery and exploitation of a buffer overflow in a 1994 Amiga FTP client, demonstrating classic stack exploitation principles.

talks.title: Reproductive Justice in the Age of Digital Surveillance
talks.teaser: EFF and privacy advocates discuss legal defense strategies, app telemetry risks, and technological protections for healthcare privacy in post-Dobbs America.
talks.summary:
Digital Surveillance of Healthcare Data

Following the overturning of federal abortion protections in the United States, location data brokers, messaging apps, and health tracking platforms face increased subpoena and surveillance scrutiny.

Threat Modeling Location Data and Health Apps

Privacy advocates and EFF researchers analyze how geolocation logs, search history queries, and period tracking applications can be weaponized in legal investigations.

State and Federal Legislative Battles

The panel examines emerging state shield laws, federal privacy proposals, and practical encryption standards designed to protect patient and provider communications.

Actionable Security Guidance for Advocates and Technologists

Panelists provide concrete technical recommendations for adopting encrypted communications, disabling behavioral advertising identifiers, and supporting privacy-focused health platforms.

talks.title: Private Until Presumed Guilty
talks.teaser: Criminal defense experts examine digital forensic extraction tools used by law enforcement, highlighting Fourth Amendment limitations and digital evidence flaws.
talks.summary:
The Ubiquity of Mobile Device Forensics

Law enforcement agencies routinely utilize advanced forensic extraction hardware and software (such as Cellebrite and GrayKey) to acquire full filesystem dumps from seized smartphones.

Auditing Forensic Extraction Reports

Allison Young and Diane Akerman review real-world digital forensic reports, exposing common analytical errors, misattributed timestamps, and context stripping during automated evidence parsing.

Fourth Amendment Realities in Digital Searches

Analyzing broad digital search warrants reveals the widening gap between traditional Fourth Amendment particularity requirements and the unrestrained extraction of cloud and local device data.

Technical Defenses and Evidentiary Scrutiny

The speakers urge defense attorneys and security researchers to rigorously scrutinize forensic tool outputs, challenge overbroad warrants, and advocate for strict digital privacy standards.

talks.title: Private Keys in Public Places
talks.teaser: Tom Pohl uncovers hardcoded private keys, certificates, and static AES encryption keys across Netgear, Fortinet, and Dell firmware, enabling universal vCenter compromise.
talks.summary:
Hardcoded Secrets Across Commercial Firmware

Despite decades of security best practices, enterprise firmware and software binaries continue to ship with embedded private keys, CA certificates, and static cryptographic secrets.

Extracting PEM Keys and Obfuscated Fortinet Archives

Tom Pohl demonstrates automated discovery techniques for extracting PEM keys from Netgear routers and unpacking custom obfuscated firmware archives in Fortinet enterprise firewalls.

Universal vCenter Decryption in Dell Enterprise Software

Dissecting Dell software revealed a hardcoded static AES encryption key used to encrypt VMware vCenter administrator credentials, allowing universal credential decryption across all customer deployments.

Fixing Systemic Key Management Failures

Pohl emphasizes the necessity of automated static binary secret scanning in CI/CD pipelines, proper hardware security modules (HSMs), and eliminating hardcoded cryptographic trust.

talks.title: Shall We Play a Game: AI in Military Systems
talks.teaser: DoD Chief Digital and AI Officer Dr. Craig Martell examines the risks of military LLM adoption and the critical role of hackers in ensuring AI accountability.
talks.summary:
40 Years After WarGames: The Reality of Military AI

Commemorating the 40th anniversary of the classic film 'WarGames', DoD Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Officer Dr. Craig Martell reflects on historical NORAD false alarms and automated decision-making.

The Seduction and Dangers of Large Language Models

Dr. Martell addresses the rapid hype surrounding Large Language Models (LLMs), warning against conflating probabilistic text generation with reliable, deterministic reasoning in high-stakes environments.

Balancing Agility with Strict Accountability

Integrating artificial intelligence across defense operations demands rigorous testing, clear provenance validation, and robust human-in-the-loop safeguards to prevent unintended escalation.

The Essential Role of the Hacker Community

The Department of Defense calls on independent security researchers and red teams to stress-test military AI models, expose adversarial vulnerabilities, and ensure responsible technology adoption.

talks.title: Power Corrupts, Corrupt It Back! Hacking Data Center Power Management
talks.teaser: Uncovers nine vulnerabilities across enterprise Power Distribution Units (PDUs) and Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) appliances, enabling physical power disruption.
talks.summary:
The Overlooked Physical Infrastructure of Data Centers

While cloud security focuses on virtualized workloads and IAM permissions, data center physical power distribution and environmental controls represent critical single points of failure.

Auditing Enterprise PDUs and DCIM Systems

Patrick Quinn and Gary Chick conduct in-depth vulnerability research against leading commercial Power Distribution Units (PDUs) and Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) appliances.

Discovering Nine Critical Vulnerabilities

The researchers disclose nine vulnerabilities—spanning unauthenticated remote code execution, command injection, and insecure firmware updates—that allow remote control over electrical circuits.

Simulating Cascading Power Disruptions and Mitigations

Demonstrating coordinated outlet cycling and transformer load surges illustrates how compromising power management can physically damage data center hardware and trigger cascading outages.

talks.title: Polynonce: An ECDSA Attack and Polynomial Dance
talks.teaser: Nils Amiet and Marco Macchetti introduce Polynonce, a novel cryptanalytic attack recovering ECDSA private keys from nonce bias across Bitcoin and Ethereum.
talks.summary:
Vulnerabilities in ECDSA Nonce Generation

Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) security hinges upon using a perfectly uniform, secret random nonce for every signature generated by a private key.

Introducing the Polynonce Attack

Nils Amiet and Marco Macchetti present Polynonce, a novel algebraic cryptanalysis attack that solves for private keys when nonces are generated by flawed pseudorandom number generators.

Scanning the Bitcoin and Ethereum Blockchains

Applying the Polynonce attack against historical transaction datasets across the Bitcoin and Ethereum public ledgers uncovered dozens of vulnerable wallet addresses.

Open-Source Implementation and Defenses

The authors release open-source verification code and an academic paper, urging developers to adopt RFC 6979 deterministic nonce generation to prevent catastrophic key recovery.

talks.title: Physical Attacks Against Smartphones
talks.teaser: Christopher Wade details physical hardware attacks on Android smartphones, exploiting custom Recovery modes and Secondary Bootloader USB flaws for root code execution.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Physical Smartphone Access

Android operating systems integrate hardware-backed disk encryption and verified boot chains, but low-level pre-boot environments remain vulnerable to physical manipulation.

Exploiting Vendor Recovery Modes via MicroSD

Christopher Wade demonstrates vulnerabilities in customized Android Recovery implementations that permit root privilege escalation and direct storage traversal using a malicious MicroSD card.

Secondary Bootloader USB Stack Exploitation

Auditing the secondary bootloader (SBL) of a major smartphone manufacturer uncovered a critical memory corruption flaw in its core USB protocol handler.

Booting Modified Android Images Without Bootloader Unlocking

Leveraging the USB vulnerability allows executing arbitrary payload code during pre-boot, enabling researchers to boot modified Android system images without compromising data integrity.

talks.title: Attacking And Securing the Pixel Modem
talks.teaser: Google Android Red Team details offensive security evaluations of Pixel smartphone baseband modems using SDRs to discover remote cellular vulnerabilities.
talks.summary:
The High-Stakes Threat Model of Smartphone Modems

Cellular baseband processors operate as highly privileged, independent system components that parse complex, unauthenticated wireless radio signals directly from cell towers.

Democratizing Baseband Research with Software-Defined Radio

Farzan Karimi, Xingyu Xing, and Eugene Rodionov explain how modern SDR toolkits and open-source cellular stacks enable researchers to audit previously opaque proprietary modem codebases.

Offensive Evaluation of Google Pixel Modems

The Android Red Team outlines their methodology for fuzzing over-the-air LTE and 5G protocol parsers, memory isolation boundaries, and inter-processor communication channels on Pixel devices.

Proactive Defense and Hardening Modems

Implementing compiler-level exploit mitigations, memory sanitizers, and rigorous internal red-teaming ensures critical baseband flaws are eliminated prior to consumer device release.

talks.title: Leveraging macOS Networking Frameworks to Heuristically Detect Malware
talks.teaser: Patrick Wardle leverages overlooked low-level macOS APIs and private frameworks to build open-source host network monitoring tools for generic malware detection.
talks.summary:
Network Telemetry as a Malware Detection Heuristic

Because nearly all macOS malware strains communicate over the network for command-and-control or exfiltration, host-level network inspection provides a universal detection signal.

Overcoming the Lack of Native macOS Network Tooling

While Windows offers mature packet filtering and event tracing frameworks, macOS historically lacked accessible, programmatic APIs for comprehensive socket and process attribution.

Deep Dive into Low-Level macOS Networking APIs

Patrick Wardle explores private frameworks, NetworkExtension providers, and kernel socket filters to programmatically inspect live network states, DNS queries, and traffic statistics.

Generic Detection of Known and Zero-Day Threats

Demonstrating open-source implementations illustrates how behavioral network telemetry generically detects both known APT malware and novel zero-day macOS threats without brittle signatures.

talks.title: Ndays Are Also 0days: The Chromium Downstream RCE Window
talks.teaser: Demonstrates transforming publicly patched Chromium N-day vulnerabilities into remote code execution 0-days across popular Electron and CEF desktop applications.
talks.summary:
The Pervasiveness of Chromium in Downstream Software

Frameworks like Electron and Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF) embed Chromium into hundreds of popular desktop communication, gaming, and productivity applications.

The 14-Week Chromium Disclosure Window

Bohan Liu, Zheng Wang, and GuanCheng Li evaluate the 'RCE window period'—the multi-week delay between Google publicly disclosing a Chromium fix and downstream apps updating dependencies.

Transforming N-Day Flaws into 10+ Desktop RCE 0-Days

Demonstrating over 10 distinct zero-day exploits shows how unpatched downstream applications allow attackers to achieve remote code execution using publicly documented V8 and WebKit bugs.

Bypassing Application Sandboxes and Best Practices

The researchers demonstrate bypassing custom application sandboxes and provide actionable patch management guidance for desktop software developers.

talks.title: mTLS: When Certificate Authentication Done Wrong
talks.teaser: Michael Stepankin analyzes implementation flaws in mutual TLS (mTLS) certificate authentication, detailing CVEs in open-source identity servers leading to impersonation.
talks.summary:
The Growing Adoption of Mutual TLS in Zero-Trust

Mutual TLS (mTLS) has become the gold standard for zero-trust client authentication and service-to-service communication, replacing passwords with cryptographic X.509 certificates.

Implementation Flaws in Certificate Validation Logic

Michael Stepankin reveals that parsing and validating client certificate attributes in application code frequently introduces critical logic vulnerabilities.

Exploiting User Impersonation and Privilege Escalation

Analyzing real-world CVEs in popular open-source identity providers and reverse proxies demonstrates how attackers can forge SAN attributes and bypass authorization filters.

Secure Code Patterns for X.509 Verification

Stepankin provides concrete source code examples and architectural guidelines for securely handling client certificates, sanitizing proxy headers, and validating certificate chains.

talks.title: Meduza: Exiled Pirate Media Outlet Breaks Through the Kremlin Propaganda Firewall
talks.teaser: Meduza CTO Alex details the technical infrastructure and circumvention engineering used to bypass Russian internet censorship and deliver unbiased news to millions.
talks.summary:
Operating an Independent Newsroom in Exile

Meduza is an independent Russian- and English-language news organization operating from Latvia, reaching millions of readers despite being designated an 'undesirable organization' by Russia.

The Rapid Rise of the Russian Sovereign Internet

Meduza's CTO Alex analyzes how Russia's state telecom regulator (Roskomnadzor) transformed one of the world's most open internet ecosystems into a centralized censorship apparatus.

Technical Warfare Against Deep Packet Inspection (DPI)

Meduza’s engineering team describes deploying custom mobile apps with built-in censorship circumvention, mirror networks, and onion routing to bypass nationwide domain blocks.

Repelling Volumetric DDoS and Protecting Staff

The presentation details defensive operations against state-backed DDoS attacks and emphasizes the vital role of technology in preserving freedom of information during wartime.

talks.title: Malware Design: Abusing Legacy Microsoft Transports and Session Architecture
talks.teaser: RJ McDown presents Obligato, a covert implant communication framework that abuses legacy Windows session architectures to decouple C2 traffic from malware processes.
talks.summary:
The Fragility of Traditional C2 Network Connections

When EDR solutions detect post-exploitation activity, forensic process-lineage analysis easily links active network sockets directly to injected implant processes, burning entire red-team infrastructures.

Introducing the Obligato Covert Transport Framework

RJ McDown presents Obligato, a specialized implant tasking and communication framework designed to break forensic process chaining and conceal persistence.

Decoupling C2 Traffic from Malware Processes

Obligato abuses legacy Microsoft RPC transports, named pipes, and Windows session architectures to disassociate network telemetry from executing payload memory.

Evading Dynamic Analysis and Resilient Re-Entry

Demonstrating advanced session multiplexing illustrates how covert implants can maintain persistent access and evade dynamic behavior monitoring on modern Windows enterprise hosts.

talks.title: What Can We Learn About Hacking in Sci-Fi?
talks.teaser: Analyzes a corpus of 200 fictional sci-fi cyberattacks against 800 real-world breaches, examining feedback loops between speculative fiction and cybersecurity development.
talks.summary:
The Feedback Loop Between Fiction and Technology

Science fiction serves as a cultural sandbox for anticipating the unintended consequences of emerging technologies, creating a feedback loop where fictional depictions actively inspire real-world engineering.

Analyzing 200 Fictional vs. 800 Real Cyberattacks

Nicolas Minvielle and Xavier Facelina construct a comparative corpus analyzing 200 fictional cyberattacks from literature, cinema, and television alongside 800 historical real-world breaches.

Assessing the Predictive Accuracy of Sci-Fi Hacking

Comparing fictional tropes against real adversary tradecraft reveals where popular narratives successfully anticipated modern cyber capabilities versus where they misinformed public perception.

Leveraging Narrative Foresight for Threat Modeling

Security teams can harness speculative storytelling and sci-fi narrative methodologies to stress-test future threat models and conceptualize novel attack surfaces before they emerge.

talks.title: Look Ma, I'm the CEO: Real-Time Video and Audio Deepfakes
talks.teaser: Demonstrates real-time executive impersonation using open-source deepfake video and audio models running on commodity GPU hardware.
talks.summary:
The Accessibility of Real-Time Synthetic Media

While generative deepfakes historically required extensive post-processing compute, modern AI frameworks enable consumer GPUs to render high-fidelity synthetic video and voice clones in real time.

Live Executive Impersonation Demonstration

Using publicly available executive keynote videos and podcast interviews, the speaker demonstrates live video and voice transformation during active video conference calls.

Social Engineering Attack Scenarios

Real-time deepfake impersonation defeats traditional voice verification and video identity checks, facilitating high-stakes CEO fraud, password resets, and fraudulent financial transfers.

Detection Frameworks and Defensive Countermeasures

Mitigating live synthetic media attacks requires multi-channel out-of-band verification, biometric liveness detection algorithms, and cryptographically signed video streams.

talks.title: LLMs at the Forefront: Pioneering the Future of Fuzz Testing
talks.teaser: Introduces FuzzForest, an open-source framework leveraging LLMs to automatically generate, repair, and triage fuzz test harnesses across Python libraries.
talks.summary:
Integrating Large Language Models into Fuzzing Workflows

While Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle with whole-system architectural reasoning, their ability to synthesize syntactically valid code makes them exceptionally suited for generating fuzz test harnesses.

Overcoming Obstacles in Automated Harness Generation

Human security researchers spend significant time writing initial fuzz harnesses and mocking complex inputs. LLMs can automate harness construction, input synthesis, and triage analysis.

Introducing FuzzForest for Python Libraries

The author introduces FuzzForest, an open-source tool that prompts LLMs to generate and iteratively repair Python fuzzers based on runtime crash feedback.

Discovering Dozens of Bugs in Top Open-Source Projects

Deploying FuzzForest across the 20 most popular open-source Python repositories uncovered dozens of previously undiscovered memory-safety, logic, and parsing bugs.

talks.title: Lions & Tigers and Fancy Bears, Oh My! A Cautionary Tale
talks.teaser: CISA Director Jen Easterly and Yale Professor Scott Shapiro discuss the history of major cyber intrusions and the necessity of Secure-by-Design engineering.
talks.summary:
Lessons from Five Decades of Cyber Intrusions

CISA Director Jen Easterly and Yale Law Professor Scott Shapiro review pivotal historical hacks, tracing how systemic architectural vulnerabilities enabled widespread nation-state espionage.

Moving Beyond Blaming the User

The speakers argue that the cybersecurity industry has historically placed an unfair burden on end-users through security awareness training rather than demanding secure software development from vendors.

The Secure-by-Design Imperative

CISA’s Secure-by-Design initiative urges software manufacturers to eliminate entire classes of vulnerabilities (such as memory-safety flaws and default credentials) before products ship.

Building Public-Private Accountability

Fostering long-term systemic resilience requires policy frameworks that align market incentives with rigorous software transparency, corporate accountability, and open vulnerability disclosure.

talks.title: J4 Gate: The Hustler Poker Cheating Scandal Investigation
talks.teaser: Scott Melnick recounts his technical investigation into the infamous Hustler Casino Live $240K poker hand, examining live-stream RFID security and cheating hypotheses.
talks.summary:
The Infamous Hustler Casino Live $240K Hand

In September 2022, an unprecedented all-in call for a $240,000 cash pot on the Hustler Casino Live stream ignited accusations of high-tech cheating across the international poker community.

Investigating Live-Stream Table RFID Architecture

Scott Melnick conducts a technical forensic analysis of broadcast poker tables, evaluating the RFID readers, embedded table antennas, production video feeds, and backstage employee access controls.

Evaluating Potential Cheating Vectors and Collusion

The investigation explores potential exploit vectors, including compromised RFID card telemetry, covert vibrating wearables, rogue wireless transmitters, and insider collusion.

Lessons in Community Sleuthing and Integrity

Melnick shares insights from 26 years in the hacker community, illustrating how open-source investigative methods and peer collaboration uncover technical anomalies in live gaming environments.

talks.title: Internet Censorship: What Governments Have in Store for You
talks.teaser: A panel of international technologists and digital rights advocates examine escalating state internet censorship, legal crackdowns, and circumvention tools.
talks.summary:
The Global Erosion of Internet Freedom

Authoritarian regimes and backsliding democracies alike are enacting restrictive telecommunications laws, centralized internet kill switches, and aggressive filtering apparatuses to control citizen information access.

Technological Mechanisms of State Censorship

Panelists analyze the deployment of nationwide Deep Packet Inspection (DPI), DNS poisoning, BGP route manipulation, and targeted throttling against independent media and privacy tools.

Legal and Regulatory Pressures on Encryption

Governments increasingly introduce legislation targeting end-to-end encrypted messaging, open-source privacy software, and VPN providers under the guise of public safety.

Building Resilient Circumvention Ecosystems

The session emphasizes the necessity for global hacker collaboration in developing decentralized, pluggable transport protocols and censorship-resistant communication infrastructure.

talks.title: Unparalleled RDP Monitoring Reveals Attackers' Tradecraft
talks.teaser: Gozint and ESET researchers use PyRDP to record and classify over 100 hours of attacker sessions on exposed RDP honeypots into behavioral archetypes.
talks.summary:
The Primacy of RDP in Ransomware Intrusions

Exposed Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) services represent one of the most frequent initial access vectors exploited by cybercriminals and opportunistic ransomware operators.

Deploying PyRDP for In-Depth Session Interception

Maxime Bergeron and Olivier Bilodeau deploy PyRDP, an open-source man-in-the-middle RDP proxy that records keystrokes, clipboard transfers, mapped drives, and video playback of live intrusions.

Categorizing Attacker Archetypes via D&D Taxonomy

Analyzing over 100 hours of video recordings reveals distinct behavioral archetypes—ranging from noisy brute-force 'Barbarians' to stealthy reconnaissance 'Rangers' and proxying 'Wizards'.

Translating Honeypot Telemetry into Blue-Team Defenses

Documenting common command sequences, tooling artifacts, and monetization strategies enables defensive teams to build robust detection rules against real-world lateral movement.

talks.title: HL7Magic: Medical Data Hacking Made Easy
talks.teaser: Katie Inns introduces HL7Magic, an open-source Burp Suite extension enabling security researchers to intercept, decode, and tamper with legacy HL7 medical device traffic.
talks.summary:
The Insecurity of Legacy Healthcare Protocols

While modern healthcare APIs adopt HTTP-based FHIR standards, critical hospital systems and embedded diagnostic devices still rely universally on legacy Health Level Seven (HL7) protocol formats.

The Lack of Tooling for Proprietary Medical Protocols

HL7 messages utilize bespoke non-HTTP framing that cannot be natively inspected, parsed, or modified by standard commercial penetration testing suites.

Introducing the HL7Magic Burp Suite Extension

Katie Inns presents HL7Magic, an open-source extension that intercepts raw TCP HL7 socket streams, decodes segment delimiters, and integrates seamlessly into Burp Suite's Repeater and Intruder.

Demonstrating Medical Device Vulnerabilities

Live demonstrations illustrate how tampering with HL7 patient identifiers and telemetry payloads can misattribute medical records, highlighting patient safety risks in clinical environments.

talks.title: Hacker Court Interactive Scenario
talks.teaser: An interactive courtroom simulation where DEF CON attendees act as jurors in a cybercrime trial, learning legal attribution standards and forensic evidence handling.
talks.summary:
Simulating a High-Stakes Cybercrime Prosecution

Hacker Court brings trial attorneys, forensic expert witnesses, and security researchers together in an interactive mock trial prosecuting a complex intrusion scenario.

The Challenges of Digital Attribution

Prosecutors and defense counsel spar over digital forensic artifacts, debating whether IP logs, shellcode signatures, and server telemetry constitute definitive proof or a deceptive false flag.

Crucial Evidence Handling for Incident Responders

The trial highlights the strict legal thresholds required for evidence admissibility, teaching detection and response engineers what forensic data must be preserved during an active breach.

Jury Deliberation and Verdict

The audience serves as the trial jury, evaluating circumstantial versus technical evidence to render a live verdict on the hacker's guilt or innocence.

talks.title: Hack the Future: Why Congress & White House Support AI Red Teaming
talks.teaser: White House and Congressional leaders discuss government backing for the DEF CON Generative AI Red Team exercise to evaluate commercial LLM risks.
talks.summary:
Government Collaboration with the Hacker Community

The White House, National Science Foundation, and Congressional AI Caucus formally partnered with DEF CON's AI Village to host the largest public Generative AI Red Team exercise.

Balancing Rapid AI Innovation with Emerging Risks

Austin Carson and federal leaders discuss the policy challenges of managing generative AI deployment across critical infrastructure, national security, and civil society.

Democratizing Public Trust and Safety Evaluations

Enabling thousands of independent hackers to stress-test frontier models from major AI providers creates transparent benchmarks for model hallucinations, bias, and vulnerability surfaces.

Institutionalizing Independent Red Teaming in AI Policy

The panel explores how lessons from public red-teaming exercises will inform future federal AI procurement standards and executive governance frameworks.

talks.title: Growing the Community of AI Hackers with the Generative Red Team
talks.teaser: AI Village organizers share the architecture and methodology behind the largest public Generative AI Red Team challenge testing frontier models at DEF CON 31.
talks.summary:
Organizing the Largest Public AI Red Teaming Event

The AI Village at DEF CON 31 assembled frontier models from Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI, Stability AI, and others on an evaluation platform built by Scale AI.

Shifting Beyond Prompt Injections and Jailbreaks

Sven Cattell, Rumman Chowdhury, and Austin Carson explain that evaluating Large Language Models requires testing stochastic behaviors, demographic biases, and hallucination propagation.

The Evolution of Algorithmic and Bias Bounties

The organizers trace the history of algorithmic bounty programs, detailing how probabilistic software flaws require reimagined bug reporting, verification, and payout structures.

Building an Inclusive Global AI Security Community

Providing accessible red-teaming platforms empowers multidisciplinary researchers to develop standardized methodologies for auditing foundation AI models.

talks.title: GhostToken: Exploiting GCP to Create Unremovable Trojan Apps
talks.teaser: Tal Skverer details GhostToken, a critical zero-day vulnerability in Google Cloud Platform allowing third-party OAuth apps to become invisible and unremovable.
talks.summary:
OAuth 2.0 Integrations in Enterprise Cloud Platforms

Modern SaaS ecosystems rely heavily on third-party OAuth applications, where users grant scoped API tokens allowing external services to access email, documents, and cloud storage.

The Architectural Coupling of Google Accounts and GCP

Tal Skverer analyzes Google's migration requiring all third-party marketplace applications to be tethered to underlying Google Cloud Platform (GCP) developer projects.

Discovering the GhostToken Zero-Day Vulnerability

Manipulating GCP project deletion states places third-party OAuth applications into an unlisted 'pending deletion' limbo where valid access tokens persist indefinitely while disappearing from user management dashboards.

Creating Permanent, Invisible Backdoor Access

Exploiting GhostToken enabled an attacker to maintain persistent, unremovable access to a victim's Google Workspace data without any visible indicator in account security settings.

talks.title: Getting a Migraine: Unique SIP Bypass on macOS
talks.teaser: Discloses 'Migraine', a novel macOS System Integrity Protection (SIP) bypass vulnerability allowing root users to load unsigned kernel extensions.
talks.summary:
The Security Boundary of macOS System Integrity Protection

System Integrity Protection (SIP) restricts root-level capabilities in macOS, preventing the modification of core system binaries, filesystem trees, and the loading of unsigned kernel extensions.

Reverse Engineering Apple Migration Assistant

Nir Even Or, Phil Pearse, and Ankur Bohra audit macOS system maintenance daemons, discovering critical logic oversights in how Apple's Migration Assistant executes elevated maintenance routines.

Bypassing SIP to Install Undeletable Malware

Exploiting the 'Migraine' vulnerability allows an attacker with root privileges to completely bypass SIP enforcement, modify protected directories, and load arbitrary kernel extensions.

Detection Strategies and Vendor Remediation

The researchers present behavioral detection heuristics for endpoint monitoring and review Apple's coordinated security patch.

talks.title: Game Changing Advances in Windows Shellcode Analysis
talks.teaser: Dr. Bramwell Brizendine introduces SHAREM, an advanced shellcode emulation framework providing complete code coverage and flawless Ghidra disassembly.
talks.summary:
The Difficulties of Analyzing Obfuscated Shellcode

Malicious shellcode frequently employs custom encoding, environment hashing, and dynamic API resolving, causing static disassemblers like IDA Pro and Ghidra to produce incomplete or corrupted output.

Introducing the SHAREM Emulation Engine

Dr. Bramwell Brizendine, Austin Kersten, and Max Hince present SHAREM, a specialized emulation framework capable of emulating over 20,000 Windows API functions and 99% of system calls.

Achieving Complete Code Coverage via Snapshot Restores

SHAREM records CPU register contexts and memory state at every control flow fork; when execution terminates, it restores previous states to explore all divergent code branches.

Flawless Disassembly and Ghidra Plugin Integration

Integrating SHAREM’s runtime emulation data with a custom Ghidra plugin automatically resolves decoded shellcode, reconstructs obfuscated strings, and labels identified API calls.

talks.title: From Feature to Weapon: Breaking Microsoft Teams and SharePoint
talks.teaser: Dr. Nestori Syynimaa abuses SharePoint Online migration APIs to tamper with files, inject stored XSS, and escalate privileges across Microsoft Teams and Azure AD.
talks.summary:
SharePoint Online as Universal Enterprise Storage

Microsoft SharePoint Online (SPO) serves as the foundational file repository for Microsoft 365, powering backend document management for Teams channels, OneDrive, and Office Groups.

Abusing Granular Migration APIs

Dr. Nestori Syynimaa audits Microsoft migration utilities (Migration Manager and SPMT), discovering that their underlying REST APIs lack strict tenant-level integrity verification.

Tampering with Shared Files and Injecting Stored XSS

An unprivileged tenant user can leverage migration endpoints to overwrite existing documents, forge file creation timestamps, and inject malicious scripts into SharePoint lists.

Cross-Service Privilege Escalation to Azure AD

Triggering stored XSS within Microsoft Teams and SharePoint execution contexts enables stealing administrative access tokens, leading to full tenant elevation of privilege in Azure Active Directory.

talks.title: Fireside Chat with the National Cyber Director
talks.teaser: Acting National Cyber Director Kemba Walden discusses the implementation of the National Cybersecurity Strategy, workforce development, and public-private defense.
talks.summary:
This DEF CON talk covers fireside chat with the national cyber director.
