talks.title: Fantastic Ethertypes and Where to Find Them
talks.teaser: Ricky Lawshae explores esoteric non-IP Ethernet protocols across transportation, industrial SCADA, and healthcare networks, demonstrating packet injection vectors.
talks.summary:
Exploring Beyond the TCP/IP Protocol Stack

While most security monitoring focuses exclusively on IP-based traffic, Layer 2 Ethernet frames support hundreds of specialized, non-routable protocols defined by distinct EtherType fields.

Surveying Esoteric Ethertypes in the Wild

Ricky Lawshae investigates obscure Ethernet protocols deployed in industrial manufacturing plants, rail transportation networks, and hospital clinical facilities.

Security Implications of Unauthenticated Layer 2 Protocols

Many specialized EtherType implementations lack basic authentication, encryption, or sequence validation, allowing local network attackers to inject control commands directly.

Defensive Visibility and Network Segmentation

The presentation demonstrates packet crafting tools for auditing non-IP protocols and provides network architecture recommendations for Layer 2 filtering.

talks.title: Exploring Linux Memory Manipulation for Stealth and Evasion
talks.teaser: Carlos Polop and Javier Gutierrez demonstrate novel in-memory manipulation techniques on Linux to execute stealthy payloads within read-only and distroless containers.
talks.summary:
Exploitation Challenges in Hardened Linux Environments

Modern container deployments increasingly utilize read-only root filesystems, `noexec` volume mounts, and minimal distroless base images to restrict attacker payload execution.

Manipulating Linux Memory Without Executable Disk Files

Carlos Polop and Javier Gutierrez explore advanced in-memory execution primitives, abusing `ptrace`, `/proc/self/mem`, and fileless shared memory file descriptors (`memfd_create`).

Process Injection and Runtime Code Patching

Step-by-step demonstrations illustrate how malicious implants can inject shellcode into running daemon memory spaces, hook dynamic symbols, and evade container security monitors.

Mitigations and Container Hardening

The authors discuss defensive countermeasures, including restricting `ptrace_scope`, deploying Seccomp system call filters, and implementing kernel-level memory integrity auditing.

talks.title: Exploiting OPC UA: Practical Attacks Against OPC UA Architectures
talks.teaser: Claroty Team82 reveals critical vulnerabilities across OPC UA protocol stack implementations, demonstrating remote code execution across industrial SCADA networks.
talks.summary:
OPC UA as the Backbone of Industrial Automation

Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture (OPC UA) is the industry standard protocol connecting physical OT sensors, SCADA servers, and corporate IT management networks.

Auditing OPC UA Protocol Stack Implementations

Noam Moshe and Sharon Brizinov conduct an extensive two-year evaluation of major commercial and open-source OPC UA stacks powering millions of industrial devices.

Uncovering Critical Protocol Specification Pitfalls

Fuzzing complex protocol features—including method invocations, message chunking, certificate validation, and complex data variants—revealed multiple RCE and DoS zero-days.

Releasing Open-Source Exploitation Tooling

The researchers release an open-source auditing framework, providing OT asset owners and equipment vendors with tools to verify and patch OPC UA deployments.

talks.title: ELECTRONizing macOS Privacy: A New Weapon in Your Red Teaming Armory
talks.teaser: Wojciech Reguła demonstrates hijacking Electron application configurations on macOS to inherit high-privilege TCC permissions without zero-days.
talks.summary:
The Privacy Architecture of macOS TCC

Apple's Transparency, Consent, and Control (TCC) subsystem enforces strict sandboxing on macOS, requiring explicit user authorization to access files, webcams, microphones, and screens.

The Inherent Vulnerabilities of Ubiquitous Electron Apps

Wojciech Reguła identifies that widely used Electron desktop applications (such as Slack, Teams, and Discord) hold extensive TCC entitlements granted by users.

Abusing Default Electron Configurations to Inherit Permissions

Manipulating insecure runtime flags, dynamic node integration parameters, and environment variables allows executing arbitrary code inside existing Electron processes to inherit their TCC rights.

Releasing Open-Source Tooling for Red and Blue Teams

Reguła releases an open-source exploitation tool for red teams while providing SOC defenders with endpoint detection telemetry rules to flag Electron process tampering.

talks.title: Defending KA-SAT
talks.teaser: Viasat engineers share the inside story of responding to the 2022 AcidRain wiper attack against the KA-SAT satellite network during the invasion of Ukraine.
talks.summary:
The Historic Cyberattack on the KA-SAT Satellite Network

In February 2022, coinciding with the Russian military invasion of Ukraine, an adversary launched a devastating destructive cyberattack against Viasat's European KA-SAT network.

Rapid Forensic Analysis of Impacted Satellite Terminals

Mark Colaluca and Nick Saunders describe how Viasat engineers conducted emergency hardware forensics, discovering within 36 hours that terminal flash memory had been overwritten by a wiper.

Reverse Engineering the AcidRain Wiper

Reverse engineering the malicious toolkit revealed a targeted wiper designed to overwrite MTD storage partitions and brick tens of thousands of satellite ground modems.

Mitigating Ongoing Electronic and Network Assaults

The authors detail how operational teams defended against sustained over-the-air network attacks for weeks following the initial incident to restore critical European communications.

talks.title: Defender Pretender: When Windows Defender Updates Become a Security Risk
talks.teaser: Discloses a zero-day vulnerability in Windows Defender signature updates, allowing unprivileged users to neutralize EDR protections and run malware fully undetected.
talks.summary:
The Critical Role of Antivirus Signature Updates

Endpoint security engines rely on continuous signature definition updates to identify emerging threats, requiring robust cryptographic validation of downloaded signature files.

Reverse Engineering Windows Defender Update Mechanisms

Omer Attias and Amit Bar dissect the internal architecture of Windows Defender, analyzing the proprietary signature database format and local update validation pipelines.

Unprivileged EDR Neutralization via Defender-Pretender

Discovering a critical logic flaw allows unprivileged users to inject manipulated signature definitions, completely neutralizing threat detection and allowing known malware to execute undetected.

Coercing Defender into Destructive File Deletion

The researchers demonstrate weaponizing Defender's remediation engine to force the deletion of critical operating system files, resulting in an unrecoverable system crash.

talks.title: Defeating VPN Always On
talks.teaser: Maxime Clementz evaluates Windows VPN Always-On enterprise security controls, demonstrating design and implementation bypasses to reach untrusted networks.
talks.summary:
The Purpose of VPN Always-On Enterprise Controls

Organizations enforce 'VPN Always-On' policies on mobile corporate laptops to ensure all network traffic is encrypted and routed exclusively through corporate security gateways.

Auditing Windows Network APIs and Commercial VPN Clients

Maxime Clementz examines how the Windows networking stack and popular commercial enterprise VPN solutions enforce persistent gateway routing rules.

Discovering Design and Implementation Bypasses

Analyzing DNS resolution flows, local subnet routing exceptions, and captive portal helper daemons reveals methods to bypass network tunneling and reach local networks directly.

Hardening Always-On VPN Deployments

Clementz provides actionable hardening configurations for enterprise network administrators to close routing leakage paths and secure endpoints on untrusted public Wi-Fi.

talks.teaser: Long-time organizers and community members welcome newcomers to DEF CON, sharing tips, cultural norms, and strategies to navigate the world's largest hacker convention.

talks.title: Staying Undetected Using the Windows Container Isolation Framework
talks.teaser: Daniel Avinoam reverse engineers the Windows Containers minifilter driver, weaponizing native filesystem isolation to hide malicious files and evade EDR sensors.
talks.summary:
The Native Architecture of Windows Containers

Introduced in Windows Server 2016, Windows Containers provide lightweight process-level and Hyper-V filesystem isolation using a built-in kernel minifilter driver.

Reverse Engineering the Container Minifilter Driver

Daniel Avinoam reverse engineers Microsoft's container storage driver, detailing how copy-on-write redirection transparently separates container file modifications from the host volume.

Weaponizing Container Isolation for EDR Evasion

Instead of attempting container escapes, an attacker can intentionally run implants inside a custom container context, blinding host-based EDR agents from observing file drop and execution events.

Releasing Open-Source Tooling and Defensive Strategies

Avinoam releases an open-source proof-of-concept tool demonstrating native container abuse and outlines telemetry signatures for security engineers to detect containerized evasion.

talks.title: Contactless Overflow: Code Execution in Payment Terminals & ATMs
talks.teaser: Josep Rodriguez demonstrates contactless buffer overflow vulnerabilities in NFC payment readers across major ATM and POS brands, enabling ATM jackpotting.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Contactless NFC Payment Readers

NFC payment terminals deployed across major retail stores, gas pumps, and ATMs must parse complex Application Protocol Data Units (APDUs) from unauthenticated wireless taps.

Discovering APDU Buffer Overflows Across Major Vendors

Josep Rodriguez analyzes firmware across seven leading terminal vendors (including IDTech, Ingenico, Verifone, and BBPOS), uncovering memory corruption bugs in APDU parsers.

Compromising Terminals via Malicious Android Taps

Using a custom Android application, an attacker can transmit malformed APDUs during an NFC exchange, executing arbitrary shellcode on bare-metal and embedded Linux readers.

Chaining Host USB Exploits and ATM Jackpotting

Rodriguez demonstrates pivoting from compromised NFC readers over internal USB connections to exploit host operating system SDKs, enabling physical ATM cash dispensing jackpotting.

talks.title: Civil Cyber Defense
talks.teaser: Tiffany Rad and Austin Shamlin highlight pro-bono civil cyber defense, using OSINT and student clinics to protect human rights organizations and combat human trafficking.
talks.summary:
Protecting Vulnerable Civil Society Organizations

Non-profit organizations, investigative journalists, and human rights defenders face targeted surveillance and harassment from well-resourced adversaries despite possessing minimal IT security budgets.

The UC Berkeley Citizen Clinic Model

Tiffany Rad presents case studies from academic public-interest clinics, demonstrating how student security researchers provide threat modeling, digital hygiene, and defensive hardening to high-risk groups.

Leveraging OSINT to Disrupt Human Trafficking

Austin Shamlin outlines open-source intelligence methodologies used to assist law enforcement in tracking human trafficking rings and identifying illicit operational infrastructure.

Scaling Volunteer and Community Defense

The speakers urge the hacker community to contribute technical expertise and open-source tooling to protect vulnerable non-profit organizations operating on the front lines.

talks.title: Using SIM Tunneling to Travel at Light Speed
talks.teaser: Introduces MobileAtlas, an open-source testbed that decouples physical SIM cards from cellular modems globally to uncover international roaming and metering flaws.
talks.summary:
Challenges in Global Cellular Roaming Research

Auditing international cellular networks requires physical access to diverse carrier roaming partnerships, mobile rate plans, and geographically dispersed base stations.

Introducing the MobileAtlas SIM-Tunneling Framework

Adrian Dabrowski and Gabriel Gegenhuber present MobileAtlas, an open-source measurement platform that decouples physical SIM cards from modems via low-latency network tunnels.

Uncovering Data Metering Flaws and Free-Riding

Auditing commercial carrier roaming configurations revealed widespread traffic accounting discrepancies, enabling zero-rated data consumption and unmetered data tunneling.

Tracking Roaming Victims via Progress Tones

The authors expose widespread IPv6 firewall misconfigurations and demonstrate fingerprinting unique carrier progress audio tones to track victims across international borders.

talks.title: Calling it a 0-Day: Hacking at PBX & UC Systems
talks.teaser: Dissects enterprise Private Branch Exchange (PBX) and Unified Communications platforms, chaining Java execution and PHP decryption bugs to gain root shells.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of Enterprise Unified Communications

On-premises Private Branch Exchange (PBX) and Unified Communications (UC) systems manage voice, video conferencing, and messaging across enterprise corporate networks.

Auditing Leading Commercial PBX Platforms

The author audits two widespread enterprise PBX products, analyzing proprietary management web consoles, telephony services, and licensing mechanisms.

Chaining Vulnerabilities from Phone Emulation to RCE

Exploitation steps include spoofing VoIP phone endpoints, decrypting obfuscated proprietary PHP source files, bypassing license checks, and abusing Java `Runtime.exec()` invocations.

Hardening Enterprise Communications Infrastructure

The presentation outlines detection signatures for malicious SIP registration traffic and provides remediation guidance for securing on-premise telephony gateways.

talks.title: Contextualizing The Vulkan Leaks & State-Sponsored Offensive Ops
talks.teaser: Joe Slowik analyzes leaked Russian NTC Vulkan documentation, contextualizing state-sponsored offensive cyber programs, automated scanning, and attack infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Deconstructing the NTC Vulkan Documentation Leaks

In early 2023, leaked internal files from Russian defense contractor NTC Vulkan exposed architectural blueprints for state-sponsored cyber offensive programs including 'Scan-V' and 'Amezit'.

Automating Attack Surface Mapping and Exploitation

Joe Slowik evaluates Scan-V's automated scanning capabilities, which continuously correlate global internet infrastructure vulnerabilities to feed targeted offensive targeting pipelines.

Historical Precedents in State Signals Intelligence

Comparing Vulkan capabilities with historic disclosures—including Russia's SORM, China's Great Cannon, and US intelligence tools—reveals a decade-long trajectory toward industrial-scale cyber operations.

The Proliferation and Industrialization of Offensive Tooling

Slowik warns that state-backed cyber programs have shifted from bespoke intrusion toolkits to standardized, modular enterprise software platforms designed for persistent warfare.

talks.title: Breaking BMC: The Forgotten Key to the Kingdom
talks.teaser: NVIDIA offensive researchers detail chaining a dozen vulnerabilities in AMI MegaRAC BMCs, demonstrating remote exploitation to flash persistent implants into server SPI flash.
talks.summary:
The Baseboard Management Controller as a Critical Threat Vector

Baseboard Management Controllers (BMCs) are autonomous service processors on enterprise server motherboards that manage power states, console redirection, and remote firmware flashing.

Auditing AMI MegaRAC BMC Implementations

Alex Tereshkin and Adam Zabrocki examine the widely deployed AMI MegaRAC BMC codebase on enterprise hardware, mapping out network-accessible IPMI and HTTP management interfaces.

Chaining a Dozen Vulnerabilities to Server Firmware Control

The researchers detail an extensive exploit chain starting from zero-knowledge remote access to memory corruption, privilege escalation, and hypervisor-independent code execution.

Flashing Persistent Malicious Firmware into SPI Flash

Demonstrating permanent firmware flashing into the host server SPI flash illustrates how BMC compromise grants attackers undetectable, OS-reinstall-resilient server control.

talks.title: Badge of Shame: Breaking into Secure Facilities with OSDP
talks.teaser: Dan Petro and David Vargas disclose over a dozen cryptographic and implementation flaws in the Open Supervised Device Protocol (OSDP) securing physical access control.
talks.summary:
The Migration from Wiegand to Encrypted OSDP

Physical access control systems are rapidly replacing unencrypted legacy Wiegand wiring with the Open Supervised Device Protocol (OSDP) to encrypt communications between badge readers and controllers.

Cryptographic Pitfalls and Implementation Blunders in OSDP

Dan Petro and David Vargas uncover systemic design oversights, including flawed AES key exchange routines, plaintext fallback modes, and predictable keystreams.

Constructing In-Line Hardware MITM Interceptors

The authors present a low-cost physical pentesting tool that can be spliced behind wall-mounted RFID badge readers to passively sniff master keys and inject door-unlock commands.

Hardening Physical Access Control Networks

Remediating OSDP deployments requires disabling insecure installation modes, enforcing strict cryptographic pairing profiles, and monitoring serial bus impedance.

talks.title: Backdoor in the Core: Altering Intel x86 Instruction Set at Runtime
talks.teaser: Reverse engineers Intel CPU microcode on Goldmont cores, achieving persistent userspace microcode patching on Linux to create hardware backdoors in x86 execution.
talks.summary:
The Hidden World of CPU Microcode

Modern x86 processors translate complex assembly instructions into sequences of low-level internal micro-operations managed by proprietary, encrypted CPU microcode ROMs.

Reverse Engineering Intel Goldmont Microcode ROM

Mathias Krog and Christian Skovsende analyze Intel Atom CPU microcode, detailing custom tracing tools developed to deconstruct instruction decoding and persistence checks.

Achieving Persistent Microcode Patching from Userspace

Bypassing hardware integrity checks allows applying custom microcode patches directly from unprivileged Linux userspace without requiring vendor cryptographic signatures.

Weaponizing Microcode for Undetectable Hardware Backdoors

The authors demonstrate modifying instruction execution semantics at the hardware core level, creating an operating-system-independent backdoor that subverts kernel access controls.

talks.title: Azure B2C 0-Day: An Exploit Chain from Public Keys to Microsoft Bug Bounty
talks.teaser: John Novak details an exploit chain in Microsoft Azure AD B2C, recovering signing keys to forge administrative tokens across customer tenants and the MSRC portal.
talks.summary:
Azure Active Directory B2C Architecture

Microsoft Azure AD B2C provides customer-facing identity and access management for thousands of global enterprises, government agencies, and the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC).

Discovering Cryptographic Misuse in Token Generation

John Novak investigates the cryptographic token issuance flows in Azure B2C, identifying flawed key derivation routines that leak critical cryptographic material.

Recovering Private Keys and Forging Arbitrary Claims

Novel algebraic cryptanalysis enables recovering the internal token-signing keys, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to mint valid administrative JWTs for any tenant.

Full Tenant Compromise and MSRC Impact

Demonstrating the full exploit chain against the live MSRC bug bounty portal illustrates how an attacker could have accessed unpatched Microsoft vulnerability reports.

talks.title: Assessing Security of Certificates at Scale
talks.teaser: Cisco researchers run Batch GCD factorization across 100M+ public X.509 certificates, recovering private RSA keys from low-entropy embedded devices.
talks.summary:
Entropy Failures in Global Key Generation

Flawed pseudorandom number generators and entropy depletion during embedded device boot cycles produce RSA keys that share prime factors with other devices on the internet.

Scaling Batch Greatest Common Divisor (BGCD) Algorithms

David McGrew, Brandon Enright, and Andrew Chi develop high-performance multithreaded tools to run Batch GCD computations across more than 100 million public HTTPS certificates.

Factoring Moduli and Generating Private PEM Keys

Correlating public certificates harvested from active scanning and Certificate Transparency logs identified thousands of vulnerable RSA moduli, immediately computing their private keys.

Auditing and Remediating Weak Public Keys

The authors demonstrate automated certificate auditing pipelines, urging certificate authorities and hardware manufacturers to enforce automated pre-issuance GCD checks.

talks.title: Apple's Predicament: NSPredicate Exploitation on macOS and iOS
talks.teaser: Austin Emmitt demonstrates bypassing Apple's iOS 16 NSPredicate restrictions, achieving 100% reliable PAC bypasses and code execution in SpringBoard.
talks.summary:
The Evolution of NSPredicate Exploitation

Following the infamous FORCEDENTRY zero-click iMessage exploit, Apple introduced strict sandboxing restrictions to prevent NSPredicate from invoking arbitrary Objective-C methods.

Circumventing iOS 16 NSPredicateVisitor Protections

Austin Emmitt discovers syntax manipulation techniques in NSPredicate parsing that completely bypass Apple's AST visitor validations across iOS 16 and macOS.

Reliable Pointer Authentication Code (PAC) Bypasses

Using carefully constructed predicate trees, Emmitt scripts the Objective-C runtime to invoke arbitrary C functions with controlled arguments, achieving a 100% reliable PAC bypass.

Exploiting SpringBoard and System Services

Demonstrating live code injection into core system daemons (including SpringBoard and Preferences) illustrates stealing sensitive notifications, device telemetry, and location data.

talks.title: An Audacious Plan to Halt the Internet's Enshittification (Encore)
talks.teaser: Cory Doctorow delivers an encore analysis on the decay of monopoly web platforms, advocating for aggressive antitrust action and adversarial interoperability.
talks.summary:
Deconstructing Platform Degradation and Lock-In

Cory Doctorow explores the structural causes behind the decline of dominant digital platforms, detailing how monopoly consolidation harms users and business customers alike.

The Threat of Anti-Circumvention Laws

Corporate platforms leverage Section 1201 of the DMCA and Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) litigation to criminalize reverse engineering, scrapers, and interoperability tools.

Restoring Digital Sovereignty via Interoperability

Mandating open APIs and legal safe harbors for adversarial interoperability allows third-party developers to build privacy-respecting wrappers around incumbent services.

A Call to Action for Hacker Self-Help

Doctorow calls upon the technical community to develop aggressive self-help tools—including tracker blockers, sideloading tools, and decentralized networks—to reclaim the open web.

talks.title: All Information Looks Like Noise Until You Break the Code
talks.teaser: TSA Administrator David Pekoske, CISA Director Jen Easterly, and CNN's Sean Lyngaas discuss modernizing cybersecurity regulations for US transportation infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Cyber Threats to National Transportation Networks

America's critical pipelines, passenger rail networks, and commercial aviation infrastructure face increasing cyber reconnaissance and ransomware threats from nation-state adversaries.

Shifting from Compliance to Outcome-Based Security

TSA Administrator David Pekoske explains the agency's updated regulatory approach, moving away from rigid checklists toward requiring operators to demonstrate measurable resilience outcomes.

Public-Private Coordination and Threat Sharing

CISA Director Jen Easterly details joint government efforts to provide actionable threat intelligence and vulnerability management support to commercial transport operators.

Engaging the Hacker Community in Critical Infrastructure Defense

The panel invites independent security researchers to collaborate with federal agencies in identifying architectural vulnerabilities and stress-testing industrial transportation systems.

talks.title: Advanced ROP Framework: Pushing ROP to Its Limits
talks.teaser: Dr. Bramwell Brizendine and Davy Kusuma present ROP ROCKET, an automated ROP compiler supporting Heaven's Gate architecture switching and bad-byte gadget synthesis.
talks.summary:
Challenges in Modern Return-Oriented Programming

Constructing reliable ROP chains to bypass Data Execution Prevention (DEP) often fails due to bad character filters in target memory and limited gadget availability.

Introducing the ROP ROCKET Framework

Dr. Bramwell Brizendine and Davy Kusuma unveil ROP ROCKET, an automated ROP chain synthesis framework featuring novel code reuse and gadget transformation primitives.

Heaven's Gate Architecture Switching in ROP

ROCKET invokes specialized ROP Heaven's Gate gadgets to dynamically transition 32-bit processes into 64-bit execution mode at runtime, dramatically expanding available gadget space.

Automated Syscall Invocations and Bad-Byte Gadget Obfuscation

Using direct Windows syscalls rather than Win32 APIs enables automatic DEP bypasses, while algebraic gadget synthesis allows utilizing gadgets whose addresses contain forbidden bytes.

talks.title: A Pain in the NAS: Exploiting Cloud Connectivity to Pwn Your NAS
talks.teaser: Claroty Team82 reveals how cloud connectivity features in Western Digital and Synology NAS devices allow remote compromise and full RCE across millions of devices.
talks.summary:
The Architecture of Cloud-Connected Storage Appliances

Modern Network-Attached Storage (NAS) appliances feature cloud relay services that allow consumers to remotely access local files from mobile apps without configuring router port forwarding.

Reverse Engineering Device Cloud Pairing Protocols

Noam Moshe and Sharon Brizinov analyze the mutual authentication protocols used by Western Digital and Synology cloud platforms, discovering flawed device identifier validation.

Device Impersonation and Token Theft via Certificate Transparency

Harvesting device metadata from Certificate Transparency logs allowed the researchers to spoof NAS identities, conduct targeted phishing, and steal cloud proxy authorization tokens.

Full Remote Code Execution at Pwn2Own Toronto

Chaining device authentication flaws with local API memory corruption enabled bypassing firewalls to achieve full remote code execution across cloud-connected NAS devices.

talks.title: Review on the Less Traveled Road: 9 Years of Overlooked MikroTik Pre-Auth RCE
talks.teaser: DEVCORE researcher NiNi Chen discloses a 9-year-old pre-authentication remote code execution zero-day in MikroTik RouterOS affecting over 3 million devices.
talks.summary:
The Attack Surface of MikroTik RouterOS

MikroTik RouterOS powers over three million enterprise and ISP networking devices globally, making it a high-priority target for state-sponsored threat actors.

Analyzing IPC Mechanisms and the Nova Message Architecture

Ting-Yu Chen (NiNi) investigates the undocumented internal architecture of RouterOS, moving beyond standard Nova Message research into low-level socket callbacks and remote objects.

Discovering a 9-Year-Old Pre-Auth RCE Zero-Day

Uncovering an architectural race condition in lower-layer remote object management revealed a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw present in all active RouterOS releases since 2014.

Winning Master of Pwn and Tool Release

Chen reviews the Pwn2Own Toronto exploit implementation, releasing open-source reverse-engineering tooling to help the research community audit RouterOS systems.

talks.title: A Broken Marriage: Abusing Mixed Vendor Kerberos Stacks
talks.teaser: Ceri Coburn demonstrates privilege escalation across mixed-vendor environments where Linux/Unix MIT and Heimdal Kerberos stacks integrate with Windows Active Directory.
talks.summary:
Interoperability in Mixed-Vendor Kerberos Realms

Enterprise environments frequently integrate Linux, macOS, and Unix hosts running open-source MIT or Heimdal Kerberos stacks into Windows Active Directory domains.

Proprietary Extensions vs. Open Protocol Standards

Ceri Coburn highlights fundamental architectural incompatibilities between Microsoft's proprietary Kerberos PAC extensions and standard POSIX identity mapping in open-source Kerberos stacks.

Exploiting Identity Discrepancies for Cross-Platform Elevation

Exploiting configuration weaknesses in domain-joined Linux systems allows attackers to forge authorization attributes, escalating privileges across Unix endpoints joined to Active Directory.

Enhancing Rubeus for Mixed-Vendor Exploitation

Coburn demonstrates an updated release of the Rubeus toolkit, equipping red-team operators with automated capabilities to exploit cross-realm Kerberos delegation flaws.

talks.title: #NoFilter: Abusing Windows Filtering Platform for Privilege Escalation
talks.teaser: Ron Ben Yizhak introduces #NoFilter, a novel privilege escalation technique abusing the Windows Filtering Platform to achieve SYSTEM execution without token manipulation.
talks.summary:
The Limitations of Classic Windows Privilege Escalation

Traditional tools that escalate to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM (such as Potato exploits and token stealers) manipulate access tokens and service handles, making them heavily monitored by EDR rules.

Reverse Engineering the Windows Filtering Platform (WFP)

Ron Ben Yizhak explores the built-in Windows Filtering Platform kernel subsystem, examining the Base Filtering Engine (BFE), TCPIP driver interfaces, and IPSec configuration.

Abusing RPC Methods for Undetected Execution

By manipulating undocumented RPC methods exposed by WFP system services, an unprivileged user can coerce kernel components to execute arbitrary processes as SYSTEM.

Evading Modern EDR Detections with #NoFilter

Demonstrating the open-source #NoFilter tool shows how abusing native network filtering components achieves full local privilege escalation while remaining completely invisible to behavioral sensors.

Web Application Flaws in Malicious Infrastructure

talks.title: certmitm: Automatic Exploitation of TLS Certificate Validation Vulnerabilities
talks.teaser: Aapo Oksman introduces certmitm, an automated tool designed to discover and exploit insecure TLS client certificate validation flaws across iOS, Windows 11, and embedded devices.
talks.summary:
Persistent Insecurities in TLS Client Validation

TLS remains the industry standard for encrypting network communications, yet developers and libraries continually struggle to implement rigorous certificate chain validation in client endpoints.

Introducing the certmitm Tool

Aapo Oksman presents certmitm, an open-source testing framework developed to automatically detect and exploit flawed TLS certificate verification logic during active man-in-the-middle engagements.

Demonstrating Exploits Across Modern Operating Systems

The author demonstrates practical certificate bypass attacks compromising high-profile applications on iOS and Windows 11, illustrating how insecure trust configurations expose encrypted sessions to interception.
